Subject: Discovery Recap: Reliability & graceful degradation — FinTech Co / Redwood

Hi Alicia + Daniel,

Thanks again for your time earlier — really helpful to walk through your reliability goals and the recent incidents. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on success criteria: 

Pain points you shared:
- Production incidents in Q1 and Q2 tied to autoscaling delays and a bad model rollout (two incidents in last 6 months).
- No consistent graceful degradation: when the primary model hits capacity the app returns 503 or huge latency spikes.
- Need clear observability and post-incident forensics (tracing + token-level cost breakdowns).

Current stack you described:
- Frontend service in GCP us-central1 calling a homegrown inference proxy; critical paths have strict 200ms median latency targets.
- Primary model currently hosted as a single-region endpoint; fallback logic is application-side and rudimentary.
- Internal SLO target: 99.9% availability on inference (customer-facing flows).

Success criteria you care about:
- Predictable tail latency under load (p95/p99 targets + clear degradation behavior).
- Automated graceful degradation: deterministic fallback to lighter models or cached responses rather than 503s.
- Post-deployment rollouts with canaries and quick rollback; traceable root cause for incidents.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Multi-tier serving: primary high-performance model + smaller fallback variants for graceful degradation, with automated routing policies.
- Multi-region routing & automated failover (us-central, us-east, eu-west) to mitigate region-level incidents.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown, trace hooks, and rollout dashboards; SOC2 artifacts available.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa (SE) to run a short architecture review and map a fallback strategy (Marissa, can we aim for early next week?).
2) Ben to share SOC2 summary, a deployment diagram, and a proposed mutual action plan (MMP) — attachments below.
3) Follow-up call with your SREs to validate p95/p99 targeting and test failover runbook.

Attachments included: SOC2_summary.pdf, deployment_architecture.drawio.png, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

I copied Marissa so she can scope the technical review and propose a quick POC plan. If I've missed anything or you want different priorities, call it out and I'll reprioritize.

Best,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the summary, this is great and captures the high-level ask. A few clarifications from our SRE side so Marissa has context before the architecture review: 

Incident history (high level):
- 2026-02-10: Model rollout (v3.2) caused high mem usage — OOMs on the single endpoint; mitigation required manual rollback.
- 2026-04-18: Region outage in us-central triggered retry storms; our proxy didn't circuit-break cleanly and we saw latency amplification.
- 2026-06-03: Autoscaler lag during an unexpectedly high traffic spike (marketing campaign) caused sustained 5+ minute tail latency.

Current mitigations we have: limited caching for a few endpoints, a homegrown circuit breaker with manual thresholds, and a separate read-only degraded mode that returns cached answers for specific queries. The problem is this is brittle and not automated across teams.

SLOs we try to meet:
- 99.9% availability overall; internal target for critical payment flows is 99.95%.
- p95 target 150–200ms, p99 target under 600ms for our critical flows.

Questions for Redwood before the technical session:
1) How do you handle model rollouts and automated rollback? Can you describe the canary logic and thresholds?
2) What fallback model strategy do you recommend for latency-sensitive flows? Do you support automatic model sub-selection by latency budget?
3) For region-level incidents, what is typical failover time and how do you prevent retry storms?
4) What SLAs do you offer for Dedicated vs Hosted (we're exploring both)?

I'll drop our SRE runbook snippets in a shared folder before the call. Thanks, and looking forward to Marissa's availability.

— Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Infrastructure | FinTech Co

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Reliability & graceful degradation — FinTech Co / Redwood

Alicia — great context, thanks for the incident timeline. Quick answers up front and proposed agenda for Marissa's tech review. I'll also attach the SOC2 summary and a draft mutual action plan.

Q1 — rollouts/rollback:
- Redwood supports staged rollouts with canary percentages, automated health checks (latency/error-rate windows), and automatic rollback rules. Typical canary: 5% for 30 minutes with p95/p99 & error-rate thresholds; we mirror your rollout cadence but can parameterize.

Q2 — fallback model strategy:
- Recommend a 3-tier approach for latency-sensitive flows: 1) full-precision primary model, 2) quantized/ distilled smaller model for degraded performance, 3) cached or template responses for ultra-critical paths.
- Our routing layer supports latency-budget-driven sub-selection so calls can be routed to the fastest compatible variant when tail latency starts degrading.

Q3 — region failover and retry storms:
- We provide cross-region routing with health-check-driven failover and built-in adaptive rate-limiting to prevent retry amplification. Typical failover (cold start excluded) is under 60s for our multi-region config; we can run a DR exercise with you to validate.

Q4 — SLAs:
- Hosted: best-effort latency SLAs with financial credits available for availability; typical offering focused on fast time-to-value.
- Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (customizable for committed capacity). We'll share standard SLA PDFs in the MMP.

Proposed tech-review agenda (Marissa to lead):
- Review current proxy & autoscaler interactions (15 min)
- Validate SLO targets and define p95/p99 test harness (20 min)
- Design fallback model selection and canary thresholds (25 min)
- Runbook & observability hooks required for post-incident forensics (10 min)

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: propose 60–90 min architecture review timeslots (owner: marissa_cole).
- Ben: share SOC2 summary + deployment diagram + MMP (done — attachments).
- Alicia / Daniel: share SRE runbook excerpts and an example traffic spike profile.

Proposed times for tech review: Tue 7/7 10:00–11:30 PT or Wed 7/8 13:00–14:30 PT. Marissa, any preference?

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf, deployment_architecture.drawio.png, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks — we can also set up a short demo of the graceful-degrade flow in a sandbox environment if you want to validate automatic routing and cache behaviors.

Best,
Ben
